annotations.text:
The method's stop condition is a state of the judges:
every soldier satisfied, in one pass, against a real external artifact.

Unanimous approval does not measure quality. It defines it.

Nothing here is built. loop.js still runs one soldier per round
and exits on that one verdict.
This is the design, not the state.

k = soldiers in the line, in ONE round.
R = rounds run so far.

R is unbounded, deliberately.
k is the standard, and must be chosen.

Stops: won / cancelled (run token removed) /
budget (ONLY if a target was set) / error.

With no target set the script believes it is unbounded.
The allowance still runs out - and then the run is killed
mid-round, losing the report. The graceful stop exists
only when the ceiling is explicit.
